[[No overall control]]{{efn|Liberal Democrat–Labour coalition}} | after_election = TBD | after_party = [[No overall control]] }} The '''2026 Colchester City Council election''' was held on 7 May 2026 to elect members of [[Colchester City Council]] in [[Essex]], [[England]]. This will be on the same day as other [[2026 UK local elections|local elections]]{{Cite web|title=Colchester City Council|url=https://www.colchester.gov.uk/elections/elections-2026/|website=colchester.gov.uk|access-date=30 January 2026|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|title=Local elections to proceed in Colchester on 7 May 2026 {{!}} Colchester City Council|url=https://www.new.colchester.gov.uk/news/2026/local-elections-proceed-colchester-7-may-2026|website=new.colchester.gov.uk|date=22 January 2026|access-date=30 January 2026|language=en}} and the [[2026 Essex County Council election]] (at which Colchester will elect nine county councillors). Due to ongoing [[Upcoming structural changes to local government in England|local government reorganisation]], this will be the final election to Colchester City Council before it is abolished and replaced by a successor [[unitary authority]]. Elections to the successor authority are due to take place in 2027. == Summary == ===Background=== Following the conclusion of the [[2024 Colchester City Council election|previous election]], the council stayed under no overall control, with the Conservatives the largest party, but seven seats short of an overall majority.{{Cite web|first= |last= |author-link= |first2= |last2= |author2-link= |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2024/england/councils/E07000071 |website=bbc.com |title=Colchester election result |pages= |date= |access-date=2 February 2026 |work= |publisher=[[BBC News]] |place= |archive-url= |archive-date= |language=en}} For the 2024-2025 period, a Liberal Democrat minority ran the council, with informal support from Labour and the Greens. David King (Mile End) continued as [[Leader of the council|council leader]]. A few weeks after the previous election, Lesley Scott-Boutell (Stanway) left the Liberal Democrats group to sit as an Independent, becoming the first Independent councillor on the council since 2022.{{Cite web|first=Elliot |last=Deady |author-link= |first2= |last2= |author2-link= |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/news/24355492.colchester-councillor-lesley-scott-boutell-quits-lib-dems/ |website=gazette-news.co.uk |title=Colchester councillor Lesley Scott-Boutell quits Lib Dems |pages= |date=30 May 2024 |access-date=2 February 2026 |work= |publisher=Daily Gazette |place=[[Colchester]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260202231609/https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/news/24355492.colchester-councillor-lesley-scott-boutell-quits-lib-dems/ |archive-date=2 February 2026 }} This change put the Liberal Democrats and Labour on the same number of seats (14 each). On 21 May 2025, a coalition was formed between the Liberal Democrats and Labour groups for the 2025-2026 period, with King being reconfirmed as council leader at the Annual Council Meeting on the same day.{{Cite web|first= |last= |author-link= |first2= |last2= |author2-link= |url=https://www.new.colchester.gov.uk/news/2025/new-coalition-administration-colchester-city-council#gsc.tab=0 |website=new.colchester.gov.uk |title=New Coalition Administration at Colchester City Council |pages= |date=21 May 2025 |access-date=2 February 2026 |work= |publisher=[[Colchester City Council]] |place=[[Colchester]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260202232853/https://www.new.colchester.gov.uk/news/2025/new-coalition-administration-colchester-city-council#gsc.tab=0 |archive-date=2 February 2026 }} ===Election result=== Four parties stood a full slate of 17 candidates, one in each ward. Unusually, the Conservatives stood only 16 candidates, with no candidate standing for the party in St Anne's & St John's. The recently formed [[Your Party (UK)|Your Party]] failed to stand any candidates.
